# What the four tools do to this tree, measured before the plan was amended

Taken on the branch with the four dev dependencies installed and no rule written
yet, so these are figures about the tree rather than about the rules.

## Biome's typed rules run without a TypeScript program

`noFloatingPromises`, `noMisusedPromises`, `useAwaitThenable` and
`noUnsafeTypeAssertion` all fire on Biome 2.5.15's own inference, in 1.8ms on one
file. So the ticket's "typed rules on" is available, and "no floating promise",
which the ticket lists under ast-grep, belongs to Biome: ast-grep would have to
match a call expression and guess at its type.

## The formatter's diff, and what shrank it

| Configuration | Files Biome would rewrite |
|---|---|
| Biome defaults | 65 |
| plus `quoteStyle: single`, `trailingCommas: all`, `semicolons: always`, `arrowParentheses: always` | 30 |
| plus `json.formatter.enabled: false` | 26 |

The first step is the repository's existing style written down rather than
changed: the tree is single-quoted and Biome defaults to double. The second is
`turbo.json`, which is JSONC carrying eighty lines of hand-written reasoning
about turbo's cache key, and `.mcp.json`, whose layout SEEN-098 F3 was about.
Biome compacts short arrays, so letting it own those two would reflow documents
whose layout is the documentation. JSON stays parsed, so a staged `.json` is not
an error in the hook, and unformatted. The 26 remaining are TypeScript files and
are rewritten once.

## The lint findings on the tree as it stands

Ten, in six files, after `preset: recommended` plus the three typed rules:

- `style/useImportType` x3: `apps/api/src/health.test.ts`,
  `packages/core/db/marketplaces.test.ts`, `packages/core/db/rls.test.ts`. Fixable.
- `correctness/noUnusedFunctionParameters` x2: `apps/api/src/webhooks/postmark.controller.ts`.
- `suspicious/noImplicitAnyLet` x5: that controller, `packages/core/db/rls.test.ts`,
  `packages/core/db/schema.test.ts` x2, `packages/providers/src/boundary.ts`.

`noImplicitAnyLet` is the one the compiler does not already catch: `let client;`
followed by an assignment is an evolving `any` that `noImplicitAny` permits.

## Why the plan is amended rather than the rules narrowed

Six of those ten findings are in files slice 1 does not name, and the formatter
rewrites twenty-six. The solution record's own mitigation said a rule needing a
real code change in product code would be turned off with its reason; that was
the wrong call and this note is where it is withdrawn. Turning off
`noImplicitAnyLet` and `noUnusedFunctionParameters` on the day the rule set
arrives, to avoid six lines in five files, would ship a rule set that does not
run and would make this ticket's first act an exception to itself.

So slices 1 and 2 name `apps` and `packages`, and the plan says plainly that
adopting a formatter rewrites every source file it is pointed at. `biome.json`
itself is the bound on what that means: the includes list is four directories and
two file patterns, and the twenty-six files are the measurement above rather than
a surprise at the review.

## Two other things the measurement settled

`preset: "recommended"` rather than `recommended: true`: the second is deprecated
in 2.5 and Biome says so on every run, and a rule set whose own configuration
prints a deprecation is a rule set people learn to read past.

`@ast-grep/cli` needs its postinstall script, which pnpm 10 does not run by
default: without it every invocation prints a warning about falling back to
runtime binary resolution, which would land in the hook's output. It goes in
`pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies`.

## The compiler flags cost nothing to turn on

Measured before the plan was written and restated here: every package already
typechecks under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and
`noImplicitOverride` with the workspace's own tsc 5.9.3. The flags bind what is
written after them; they repair nothing, and their fixtures are what prove each
one is on.
